items.title: Start Jupyter
items.body:
pip install jupyterlab
jupyter lab
jupyter notebook

items.title: Register a virtualenv as a kernel
items.body:
pip install ipykernel
python -m ipykernel install --user --name {{env_name}} --display-name "Python ({{env_name}})"
items.description: Use your project's environment in Jupyter.

items.title: Notebook shortcuts
items.body:
Shift+Enter   run cell and move on       Ctrl+Enter   run cell
Esc then:  A / B insert above / below   DD delete cell   M markdown   Y code
Z undo cell delete   Shift+M merge cells   Ctrl+Shift+- split at cursor

items.description: Timing, reloading modules and shell commands.

items.title: Export and clean notebooks
items.body:
jupyter nbconvert --to html notebook.ipynb
jupyter nbconvert --to pdf notebook.ipynb
jupyter nbconvert --clear-output --inplace notebook.ipynb
items.description: Convert to HTML/PDF and strip outputs before committing.

items.title: Matplotlib: line plot
items.body:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
ax.plot(x, y, label="series", color="tab:blue", linewidth=2)
ax.set_title("Title")
ax.set_xlabel("x"); ax.set_ylabel("y")
ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
ax.legend()
plt.show()
items.description: Basic figure with labels, grid and legend.

items.title: Matplotlib: scatter plot
items.body:
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
sc = ax.scatter(df["x"], df["y"], c=df["value"], cmap="viridis", alpha=0.7)
fig.colorbar(sc, label="value")
ax.set_xlabel("x"); ax.set_ylabel("y")

items.title: Matplotlib: bar chart
items.body:
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.bar(categories, values, color="tab:green")
ax.set_ylabel("count")
ax.bar_label(ax.containers[0])          # value labels
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha="right")
plt.tight_layout()

items.title: Matplotlib: histogram and boxplot
items.body:
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4))
axes[0].hist(df["age"], bins=20, edgecolor="black")
axes[0].set_title("Age distribution")
axes[1].boxplot([df[df.group == g]["score"] for g in groups])
axes[1].set_xticks(range(1, len(groups) + 1), groups)
axes[1].set_title("Score by group")

items.title: Matplotlib: subplots grid
items.body:
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(10, 8), sharex=True)
for ax, col in zip(axes.flat, ["a", "b", "c", "d"]):
    ax.plot(df[col]); ax.set_title(col)
fig.suptitle("Overview")
fig.tight_layout()

items.title: Matplotlib: save a figure
items.body:
fig.savefig("figure.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
fig.savefig("figure.pdf", bbox_inches="tight")      # vector for reports

items.title: Matplotlib: twin axes, log scale, annotation
items.body:
ax2 = ax.twinx()                    # second y axis
ax.set_yscale("log")
ax.annotate("peak", xy=(x0, y0), xytext=(x0 + 1, y0 + 5), arrowprops={"arrowstyle": "->"})
ax.axhline(0.5, linestyle="--", color="gray")
ax.set_xlim(0, 10); ax.set_ylim(0, 1)

items.title: Figure tips for reports
items.body:
- Label axes with units; add a title or caption
- Font size at least 10 pt at final print size (plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 11)
- Do not rely on colour alone (use markers/line styles); check greyscale
- Start bar charts at zero
- Save at 300 dpi or as PDF/SVG
- Refer to every figure in the text (Figure 1 shows...)
items.description: Make figures readable in a document.
